station.name: Reims-Prunay
station.note: Météo-France 'Synthèse climatologique' 2022 for Reims-Prunay, published by the Marne prefecture, printing the 1991-2020 normals. Precipitation normals are marked reconstituted; temperature normals for 1991-2012 were computed from nearby station 51183001. No sunshine normal is printed for this station, so the Sun layer was swapped for Soil.

facts.claim: Champagne AOC first recognised by decree of 29 June 1936
facts.source: INAO, cahier des charges AOC Champagne (modification draft 11 Sept 2024)

facts.claim: Atlas outline area 354,439 ha = 3,544 km², 312 communes listed
Bedrock: 80% carbonate sedimentary rocks (limestone, marl, dolomite), 17% mixed sedimentary
Slopes are chalky, marly or sandy ('crayeuses, marneuses ou sableuses')
Chalk drains well yet holds water for the vines
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas study lesson 'Champagne: region and grapes'

facts.claim: Climate: oceanic influence brings regular water; continental influence brings sometimes destructive frosts and favourable summer sun
Annual precipitation Reims-Prunay 621.4 mm vs Paris-Montsouris 634.3 mm (1991-2020)
July mean max 25.2 °C, January mean min 0.6 °C at Reims-Prunay
WSET bands: cool up to about 16.5 °C growing season average, moderate 16.5-18.5
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas study lesson 'Climate and weather'

facts.claim: Pinot Noir 38%, Chardonnay 31%, Meunier 31% of the area under vine; minor varieties at most 0.3%
Non-vintage: at least 15 months from tirage before release; vintage: at least 36 months; disgorging not before 12 months
facts.source: INAO cahier des charges IX.5.a, IX.2.e

facts.claim: Grapes must be harvested as whole bunches
